17. - **The domain has crisp, mechanically checkable traps** that make perfect eval assertions:
18.   alpha-3 country codes silently break flags, dynamic Tailwind classes silently fail,
19.   `upcoming.json` ordering, UTC-only times, placeholder `T00:00:00Z` handling.
20. - **Deterministic ground truth**: `npm run validate:data` and the pipeline unit tests give
21.   evals a real oracle, not just string matching.
22. - **A full three-layer AI config** (always-on → skills → commands → agent personas,
23.   see `docs/ai-workflows.md`) — the blog can show evals closing the loop: *authored →
24.   auto-triggered → measured*.
25. 
26. ## What waza gives us (research summary)
27. 
28. Waza is Microsoft's Go CLI for creating, testing, and measuring agent skills.
29. 
30. **Key commands**
31. 
32. | Command | Purpose |
33. |---------|---------|
34. | `waza init` / `waza new skill <name>` | Scaffold workspace / skill |
35. | `waza check <skill> [--target high --auto]` | Frontmatter compliance scoring + fix suggestions |
36. | `waza tokens count\|suggest <SKILL.md>` | Token budget check (soft 500 / hard 5,000 tokens for SKILL.md) |
37. | `waza run <skill> [-o results.json] [--parallel]` | Run eval suite; exit code 0/1/2 maps to CI pass/fail/config-error |
38. 
39. **Compliance rubric** (from waza's skill best practices):
40. 
41. | Level | Requirement |
42. |-------|-------------|
43. | Low | Description < 150 chars OR no triggers |
44. | Medium | ≥150 chars AND trigger keywords |
45. | Medium-High | Both `USE FOR:` and `DO NOT USE FOR:` sections |
46. | High | Medium-High + routing clarity (`INVOKES` / `FOR SINGLE OPERATIONS`) |
47. 
48. Our skills were written to Medium-High; **High** needs the routing-clarity additions.
49. 
50. **Eval anatomy**: `eval.yaml` (name, skill, `config:` with `trials_per_task`,
51. `timeout_seconds`, `executor: mock|copilot-sdk`, `model`), `tasks/*.yaml` (id, prompt,
52. input files, `expected.output_contains`, `expected.behavior.max_tool_calls`),
53. `fixtures/` for test data. Graders: **code** (assertions on output), **text** (regex),
54. **behavior** (tool-call constraints), plus `contains` validators. Custom agents
55. (`.agent.md`) get **automatic tool-constraint validation** via `waza run <agent-name>`.
56. 
57. **Executors**: `mock` (no API calls — CI-friendly) and `copilot-sdk` (real models via
58. `GITHUB_TOKEN` / provider env vars) — the real executor powers the model-comparison blog
59. material.
60. 
61. ## Layout decision (RESOLVED — Phase 0 spike, 2026-07-15, waza 0.38.0)
62. 
63. **Chosen: Option B without the symlink.** Waza 0.38.0's workspace detection finds
64. `.github/skills/` natively from the repo root — `waza check` (no args) scores all four
65. skills, and `waza new eval <skill>` / `waza run <skill>` use a top-level `evals/<skill>/`
66. directory. No `skills` symlink and no new config needed.
67. 
68. - Skills stay in `.github/skills/<skill>/SKILL.md` (unchanged).
69. - Eval suites live in `evals/<skill>/eval.yaml` + `evals/<skill>/tasks/*.yaml`.
70. - Verified end-to-end: `waza run astro-frontend-conventions` with `executor: mock`
71.   discovers and runs the suite (scaffold via `waza new eval`; default executor is
72.   `copilot-sdk` — flip to `mock` for CI).
73. - Pinned version: **waza 0.38.0** (installed at `~/bin/waza`).
74. - Option A (`.github/skills/<skill>/evals/`) rejected: `waza new eval`/`run` conventions
75.   assume the top-level `evals/` dir.
76. (Constraint carried over: never let a SKILL.md share a directory with an `.agent.md`.)
77. 
78. ## Phases
79. 
80. ### Phase 0 — Spike: install + workspace detection *(bd: w1)*
81. Install the CLI (`curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/microsoft/waza/main/install.sh | bash`),
82. run `waza check` against one existing skill, test Option A vs B, pin the waza version used
83. (blog reproducibility). **Exit criteria:** `waza check astro-frontend-conventions` produces
84. a score; layout chosen and documented here.
85. 
86. ### Phase 1 — Compliance baseline → High *(bd: w2)*
87. 1. Run `waza check` + `waza tokens count` on all four skills; **save the raw "before"
88.    output to `docs/waza-results/baseline/`** (first blog artifact).
89. 2. Lift each skill to **High**: add routing-clarity sections (`FOR SINGLE OPERATIONS`,
90.    `INVOKES` where applicable) without bloating past the 500-token soft limit.
91. 3. Re-run and save the "after" output. **Exit criteria:** all four at High, within token
92.    budget, before/after captured.
93. 
94. ### Phase 2 — Flagship eval suite: `add-new-series` *(bd: w3, supersedes the old cp1 scaffolding issue)*
95. The deepest suite — this is the blog centerpiece. Tasks (mock executor first):
96. 
97. | Task id | Scenario | Key graders |
98. |---------|----------|-------------|
99. | `happy-path-seed-series` | "Add the Fictional GT Trophy (id: `fgt`)" with fixture calendar data | code: seed file exists + parses; text: entry in `SERIES` map; behavior: bounded tool calls |
100. | `trap-alpha3-country` | Fixture data supplies `NLD`/`GBR` codes | output/diff must contain alpha-2 (`nl`, `gb`) — catches the silent-flag trap |
101. | `trap-dynamic-tailwind` | Series color wiring | text: forbid `bg-[#` in produced component code, require `style=` |
102. | `trap-placeholder-times` | Two sessions with unannounced times | require `T00:00:00Z` placeholders, not invented times |
103. | `routing-negative` | Prompt that should NOT trigger the skill ("fix a typo in EventCard") | behavior: skill not invoked / no seed files touched |
104. 
105. Fixtures use a **fictional series** so evals never collide with real seed data.
106. **Exit criteria:** `waza run add-new-series` passes on mock executor; suite documented.
107. 
108. ### Phase 3 — Eval suites for the other three skills *(bd: w4)*
109. 2–3 tasks each, same pattern (happy path + one trap + one anti-trigger):
110. - `seed-data-schema`: fix-a-broken-fixture task (dupe id, round gap, alpha-3) → graders
111.   assert the specific corrections; must recommend `validate:data` + silver rebuild.
112. - `astro-frontend-conventions`: scaffold-a-component task → forbid framework imports,
113.   require `astro:after-swap` init pattern and `data-local-time`.
114. - `medallion-data-pipeline`: debugging task ("Moto3 missing from dashboard") → answer must
115.   route bronze→silver→gold and name the gold rebuild, not suggest editing gold by hand.
116. **Exit criteria:** all four skills have runnable suites; one `waza run` (or four) green on mock.
117. 
118. ### Phase 4 — Agent eval: tool-constraint validation *(bd: w5)*
119. Eval `racetrack-workflow-router.agent.md` — it declares `tools: [read, search, agent]`
120. (no write). Tasks: routing prompts where the correct behavior is *delegation, not editing*.
121. Waza's automatic tool-constraint validation proves the persona can't mutate files — a
122. distinctive blog angle ("evals for agent personas, not just skills").
123. **Exit criteria:** `waza run racetrack-workflow-router` green; constraint violation
124. demonstrably fails (test once by temporarily prompting an edit).
125. 
126. ### Phase 5 — CI integration *(bd: w6)*
127. `.github/workflows/skill-evals.yml`:
128. - **PR job** (paths: `.github/skills/**`, `evals/**`, `.github/agents/**`): install waza →
129.   `waza check` all skills (fail under Medium-High) → `waza run` with `executor: mock` →
130.   upload `results.json` artifact. No secrets needed.
131. - **Optional weekly job**: real `copilot-sdk` executor with `GITHUB_TOKEN`, results
132.   committed to `docs/waza-results/` (trend data for the blog).
133. **Exit criteria:** PR touching a skill runs evals; red on failure (exit code 1).
134. 
135. ### Phase 6 — Model comparison matrix *(bd: w7)*
136. Run the flagship suite with the real executor across 2–3 models
137. (e.g. Claude vs GPT-4o — whatever the Copilot SDK setup exposes), `-o` per-model
138. results.json, build a pass-rate table per task. This is the money chart: *which traps do
139. which models fall into without the skill vs with it* — if feasible, also run with the
140. skill body blanked to measure the skill's lift.
141. **Exit criteria:** comparison table in `docs/waza-results/model-comparison.md`.
142. 
143. ### Phase 7 — Blog asset capture + docs *(bd: w8)*
144. - Collect: before/after compliance scores, token counts, eval pass matrices, model
145.   comparison, CI screenshots.
146. - Update `docs/ai-workflows.md` (evals become layer 5 of the model) and README
147.   (AI-Assisted Development section + eval badge if CI supports one).
148. - Draft blog outline (`docs/waza-results/blog-outline.md`): ① why measure skills,
149.   ② the rubric journey Low→High, ③ writing trap-based evals from real repo bugs,
150.   ④ agent tool-constraint evals, ⑤ model matrix, ⑥ CI gating.
151. **Exit criteria:** every claim in the outline backed by a committed artifact.
152. 
153. ## Task Breakdown — bd mapping
154. 
155. | Order | bd title (short) | Depends on | Priority |
156. |-------|------------------|------------|----------|
157. | w1 | Spike: install waza, pick workspace layout | — | P1 |
158. | w2 | Compliance: all 4 skills to High + token budget, before/after captured | w1 | P1 |
159. | w3 | Flagship eval suite: add-new-series (5 tasks, mock green) | w1 | P1 |
160. | w4 | Eval suites: seed-data-schema, astro-frontend-conventions, medallion-data-pipeline | w3 | P2 |
161. | w5 | Agent eval: workflow-router tool-constraint validation | w1 | P2 |
162. | w6 | CI: skill-evals.yml (check + mock run on PR, optional weekly real run) | w2, w3 | P2 |
163. | w7 | Model comparison matrix with copilot-sdk executor | w3, w6 | P2 |
164. | w8 | Blog assets: results, docs/README updates, blog outline | w4, w5, w7 | P3 |
165. 
166. ## Risks & mitigations
167. 
168. - **Waza is young and moving fast** → pin the CLI version in CI and in this doc; re-verify
169.   spec fields at implementation time (docs above were fetched 2026-07-13).
170. - **Mock executor limits realism** → treat mock as CI smoke; real judgments come from the
171.   scheduled copilot-sdk runs.
172. - **Copilot SDK auth in CI** → `GITHUB_TOKEN` per waza's CI docs; if the org setup blocks
173.   it, keep model comparison as a local-run artifact instead of CI.
174. - **`.github/skills/` isn't waza's default layout** → resolved by the Phase 0 spike;
175.   worst case a `skills` symlink (pattern already proven with `.claude/skills`).
176. - **Eval fixtures drifting into real data** → fictional series ids (`fgt`) only; never
177.   touch `data/seed/` from eval tasks.
178.

 skills, and `waza new eval <skill>` / `waza run <skill>` use a top-level `evals/<skill>/`
 directory. No `skills` symlink and no new config needed.
 
 - Skills stay in `.github/skills/<skill>/SKILL.md` (unchanged).
 - Eval suites live in `evals/<skill>/eval.yaml` + `evals/<skill>/tasks/*.yaml`.
 - Verified end-to-end: `waza run astro-frontend-conventions` with `executor: mock`
   discovers and runs the suite (scaffold via `waza new eval`; default executor is
   `copilot-sdk` — flip to `mock` for CI).
 - Pinned version: **waza 0.38.0** (installed at `~/bin/waza`).
 - Option A (`.github/skills/<skill>/evals/`) rejected: `waza new eval`/`run` conventions
   assume the top-level `evals/` dir.
 (Constraint carried over: never let a SKILL.md share a directory with an `.agent.md`.)
 
 ## Phases
 
 ### Phase 0 — Spike: install + workspace detection *(bd: w1)*
 Install the CLI (`curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/microsoft/waza/main/install.sh | bash`),
 run `waza check` against one existing skill, test Option A vs B, pin the waza version used
 (blog reproducibility). **Exit criteria:** `waza check astro-frontend-conventions` produces
 a score; layout chosen and documented here.
 
 ### Phase 1 — Compliance baseline → High *(bd: w2)*
 1. Run `waza check` + `waza tokens count` on all four skills; **save the raw "before"
    output to `docs/waza-results/baseline/`** (first blog artifact).
 2. Lift each skill to **High**: add routing-clarity sections (`FOR SINGLE OPERATIONS`,
    `INVOKES` where applicable) without bloating past the 500-token soft limit.
 3. Re-run and save the "after" output. **Exit criteria:** all four at High, within token
    budget, before/after captured.
 
 ### Phase 2 — Flagship eval suite: `add-new-series` *(bd: w3, supersedes the old cp1 scaffolding issue)*
 The deepest suite — this is the blog centerpiece. Tasks (mock executor first):
 
 | Task id | Scenario | Key graders |
 |---------|----------|-------------|
 | `happy-path-seed-series` | "Add the Fictional GT Trophy (id: `fgt`)" with fixture calendar data | code: seed file exists + parses; text: entry in `SERIES` map; behavior: bounded tool calls |
 | `trap-alpha3-country` | Fixture data supplies `NLD`/`GBR` codes | output/diff must contain alpha-2 (`nl`, `gb`) — catches the silent-flag trap |
 | `trap-dynamic-tailwind` | Series color wiring | text: forbid `bg-[#` in produced component code, require `style=` |
 | `trap-placeholder-times` | Two sessions with unannounced times | require `T00:00:00Z` placeholders, not invented times |
 | `routing-negative` | Prompt that should NOT trigger the skill ("fix a typo in EventCard") | behavior: skill not invoked / no seed files touched |
 
 Fixtures use a **fictional series** so evals never collide with real seed data.
 **Exit criteria:** `waza run add-new-series` passes on mock executor; suite documented.
 
 ### Phase 3 — Eval suites for the other three skills *(bd: w4)*
 2–3 tasks each, same pattern (happy path + one trap + one anti-trigger):
 - `seed-data-schema`: fix-a-broken-fixture task (dupe id, round gap, alpha-3) → graders
   assert the specific corrections; must recommend `validate:data` + silver rebuild.
 - `astro-frontend-conventions`: scaffold-a-component task → forbid framework imports,
   require `astro:after-swap` init pattern and `data-local-time`.
 - `medallion-data-pipeline`: debugging task ("Moto3 missing from dashboard") → answer must
   route bronze→silver→gold and name the gold rebuild, not suggest editing gold by hand.
 **Exit criteria:** all four skills have runnable suites; one `waza run` (or four) green on mock.
 
 ### Phase 4 — Agent eval: tool-constraint validation *(bd: w5)*
 Eval `racetrack-workflow-router.agent.md` — it declares `tools: [read, search, agent]`
 (no write). Tasks: routing prompts where the correct behavior is *delegation, not editing*.
 Waza's automatic tool-constraint validation proves the persona can't mutate files — a
 distinctive blog angle ("evals for agent personas, not just skills").
 **Exit criteria:** `waza run racetrack-workflow-router` green; constraint violation
 demonstrably fails (test once by temporarily prompting an edit).
 
 ### Phase 5 — CI integration *(bd: w6)*
 `.github/workflows/skill-evals.yml`:
 - **PR job** (paths: `.github/skills/**`, `evals/**`, `.github/agents/**`): install waza →
   `waza check` all skills (fail under Medium-High) → `waza run` with `executor: mock` →
   upload `results.json` artifact. No secrets needed.
 - **Optional weekly job**: real `copilot-sdk` executor with `GITHUB_TOKEN`, results
   committed to `docs/waza-results/` (trend data for the blog).
 **Exit criteria:** PR touching a skill runs evals; red on failure (exit code 1).
 
 ### Phase 6 — Model comparison matrix *(bd: w7)*
 Run the flagship suite with the real executor across 2–3 models
 (e.g. Claude vs GPT-4o — whatever the Copilot SDK setup exposes), `-o` per-model
 results.json, build a pass-rate table per task. This is the money chart: *which traps do
 which models fall into without the skill vs with it* — if feasible, also run with the
 skill body blanked to measure the skill's lift.
 **Exit criteria:** comparison table in `docs/waza-results/model-comparison.md`.
 
 ### Phase 7 — Blog asset capture + docs *(bd: w8)*
 - Collect: before/after compliance scores, token counts, eval pass matrices, model
   comparison, CI screenshots.
 - Update `docs/ai-workflows.md` (evals become layer 5 of the model) and README
   (AI-Assisted Development section + eval badge if CI supports one).
 - Draft blog outline (`docs/waza-results/blog-outline.md`): ① why measure skills,
   ② the rubric journey Low→High, ③ writing trap-based evals from real repo bugs,
   ④ agent tool-constraint evals, ⑤ model matrix, ⑥ CI gating.
 **Exit criteria:** every claim in the outline backed by a committed artifact.
 
 ## Task Breakdown — bd mapping
 
 | Order | bd title (short) | Depends on | Priority |
 |-------|------------------|------------|----------|
 | w1 | Spike: install waza, pick workspace layout | — | P1 |
 | w2 | Compliance: all 4 skills to High + token budget, before/after captured | w1 | P1 |
 | w3 | Flagship eval suite: add-new-series (5 tasks, mock green) | w1 | P1 |
 | w4 | Eval suites: seed-data-schema, astro-frontend-conventions, medallion-data-pipeline | w3 | P2 |
 | w5 | Agent eval: workflow-router tool-constraint validation | w1 | P2 |
 | w6 | CI: skill-evals.yml (check + mock run on PR, optional weekly real run) | w2, w3 | P2 |
 | w7 | Model comparison matrix with copilot-sdk executor | w3, w6 | P2 |
 | w8 | Blog assets: results, docs/README updates, blog outline | w4, w5, w7 | P3 |
 
 ## Risks & mitigations
 
 - **Waza is young and moving fast** → pin the CLI version in CI and in this doc; re-verify
   spec fields at implementation time (docs above were fetched 2026-07-13).
 - **Mock executor limits realism** → treat mock as CI smoke; real judgments come from the
   scheduled copilot-sdk runs.
 - **Copilot SDK auth in CI** → `GITHUB_TOKEN` per waza's CI docs; if the org setup blocks
   it, keep model comparison as a local-run artifact instead of CI.
 - **`.github/skills/` isn't waza's default layout** → resolved by the Phase 0 spike;
   worst case a `skills` symlink (pattern already proven with `.claude/skills`).
 - **Eval fixtures drifting into real data** → fictional series ids (`fgt`) only; never
   touch `data/seed/` from eval tasks.
 
 ## Sources
 
 - [microsoft/waza](https://github.com/microsoft/waza) — CLI/framework for agent skills
 - [Getting Started](https://github.com/microsoft/waza/blob/main/docs/GETTING-STARTED.md) — eval.yaml/task spec, graders, executors
 - [Guide](https://github.com/microsoft/waza/blob/main/docs/GUIDE.md) — workspace layouts, `waza check`, compliance levels
 - [Skills CI Integration](https://github.com/microsoft/waza/blob/main/docs/SKILLS_CI_INTEGRATION.md) — Actions workflow, exit codes, executors in CI
 - [Skill Best Practices](https://github.com/microsoft/waza/blob/main/docs/SKILL-BEST-PRACTICES.md) — frontmatter rubric, token budgets

21.   "id": "dtm-2026-r01",      // unique across ALL seed files

24.   "round": 1,                // sequential, no gaps

26.     "countryCode": "de" },   // alpha-2 ONLY — alpha-3 = empty flag
27.   "sessions": [{ "type": "race", "startTimeUTC": "2026-05-10T13:00:00Z", "endTimeUTC": "…" }],
28.   "dateStart": "2026-05-08", // = first session date

 # Seed Data Schema
 
 Seed files (`data/seed/<seriesId>.json`) are the source of truth for series without free APIs; same schema as silver (`docs/architecture.md`). `seriesId`: canonical lowercase id from `src/lib/series.ts`.
 
 ## Required fields
 
 ```jsonc
 {
   "id": "dtm-2026-r01",      // unique across ALL seed files
   "seriesId": "dtm",
   "eventName": "...",
   "round": 1,                // sequential, no gaps
   "circuit": { "name", "city", "country",
     "countryCode": "de" },   // alpha-2 ONLY — alpha-3 = empty flag
   "sessions": [{ "type": "race", "startTimeUTC": "2026-05-10T13:00:00Z", "endTimeUTC": "…" }],
   "dateStart": "2026-05-08", // = first session date
   "dateEnd": "2026-05-10",   // = last session date
   "status": "upcoming"       // | live | completed | cancelled
 }
 ```
 
 ## Time rules
 
 - **ISO 8601 UTC** (`...Z`) only; browser localizes — never store local times.
 - Unconfirmed → `T00:00:00Z` placeholder (`isPlaceholderTime()`); never invent times.
 - Moto2/Moto3 race ≈ MotoGP−2h / −4h.
 
 ## After every edit
 
 ```bash
 uv run python -m pipeline --series <id>
 npm run validate:data
 ```
 
 Rebuild gold (snippet in medallion-data-pipeline). Commit seed/silver/gold, never bronze. Bulk edits: `/seed-audit` first.
